sections.overview: The Scaly-breasted Munia is a small Asian estrildid finch; populations introduced outside its native range are established in some places.
sections.identification: Its pale underparts have dark, scale-like markings; the stout bill is adapted to seeds.
sections.habitat: It uses grassland, scrub, crops and other semi-open places, often near people.
sections.diet: Seeds make up most of its usual food; Australian observations also report occasional scavenging around farms and refuse.
sections.behavior: It forages in groups and can gather in flocks numbering hundreds outside the breeding season.
sections.reproduction: In its native Southeast Asian range, it can breed throughout the year when conditions are suitable; both sexes incubate.
sections.ecology: It forages from the ground and also hangs from stems to reach seeds.
sections.conservation: The global assessment cited by Cornell lists it as Least Concern and reports a stable trend; this does not describe every local introduced population.
